name: Haughton Crater / Haughton-Mars Project (Devon Island)
note: ~23 km, ~31 Ma impact crater in polar desert with permafrost and ground ice; HMP base camp on the NW rim has hosted NASA rover/EVA/spacesuit tests since 1997.

name: Flashline Mars Arctic Research Station (FMARS)
note: Mars Society habitat on the rim of Haughton Crater used for long-duration crewed Mars simulations (e.g., Mars 160 Arctic phase).

name: Mars Desert Research Station (Hanksville, Utah)
note: Habitat amid Jurassic–Cretaceous red-bed, gypsum and bentonite terrains of the San Rafael Swell area; >300 crew rotations of Mars EVA simulations.

name: HI-SEAS habitat (Mauna Loa)
note: Geodesic habitat at ~2,500 m on barren basaltic lava of Mauna Loa used for 4–12-month isolation/crew-cohesion studies.

name: Mauna Kea ISRU test site (Pu'u Hiwahine, PISCES)
note: Tephra/cinder-rich slopes used for regolith excavation, oxygen extraction and RESOLVE volatile-prospecting rover tests; approximate coordinates of the Pu'u Hiwahine test area.

source.label: NTRS: ISRU field tests 2010 and 2012 at Mauna Kea

name: Black Point Lava Flow (Desert RATS)
note: Basaltic flow in the San Francisco Volcanic Field where NASA tested the Space Exploration Vehicle, habitats and multi-day pressurized-rover traverses (2008–2011).

source.label: LPI Lunar Analog – Black Point Lava Flow

name: Meteor Crater (Barringer Crater)
note: Best-preserved simple impact crater on Earth (~1.2 km, ~50 ka); classic Apollo training site for crater ejecta and shock-metamorphism.

name: Craters of the Moon National Monument
note: Young basaltic lava field with lava tubes, spatter cones and rifts used for Mars basalt EVA science-operations tests (BASALT) and lunar volcanism studies (FINESSE).

name: Lava Beds National Monument
note: More than 700 lava-tube caves, some with perennial ice, used to test robotic cave mapping and cave-microbe life detection for Mars/Moon lava tubes.

name: Río Tinto (Peña de Hierro)
note: Extremely acidic (pH ~2), iron-rich river and subsurface with jarosite/hematite similar to Meridiani; used for robotic subsurface life-detection drilling.

name: AMASE – Bockfjord Volcanic Complex (Sverrefjell), Svalbard
note: Volcanoes erupted under ice host carbonate globules like those in Martian meteorite ALH84001; used to test MSL/ExoMars instruments.

name: Lanzarote (La Corona lava tube / Timanfaya)
note: UNESCO Geopark with ~8 km La Corona lava tube and young Timanfaya basalts used for ESA astronaut geology training and cave exploration.

name: Nördlinger Ries impact crater
note: ~24 km, 14.8 Ma complex crater with suevite impact breccias; ESA astronaut geology training ground.

name: Holuhraun lava field
note: 2014–15 flood-basalt eruption with fresh basaltic sand plains used as a Mars-like terrain for rover autonomy and sediment studies.

name: Pavilion Lake
note: Freshwater lake with rare modern microbialites explored with DeepWorker submersibles to rehearse science operations and biosignature search.

name: Axel Heiberg Island – Gypsum Hill perennial springs
note: Cold, hypersaline perennial springs flowing through ~600 m of permafrost at -15 C mean air temperature; analog for Martian subsurface brines.

name: Concordia Station (Dome C)
note: 3,233 m high-plateau station with ~9 months isolation, hypobaric hypoxia and winter lows near -80 C; ESA's long-duration isolation analog.

name: McMurdo Dry Valleys (Wright Valley / Lake Vanda)
note: Coldest, driest ice-free terrain on Earth with ground ice, polygons and ice-covered lakes; premier Mars periglacial and life-limit analog.

name: Don Juan Pond
note: CaCl2-saturated pond that stays liquid below -50 C; analog for deliquescent brines and recurring slope lineae.

name: Atacama Desert – Yungay
programs: NASA ASTEP Life in the Atacama
note: Hyperarid core with nitrate/perchlorate soils near the dry limit of life; used for autonomous rover drilling and biosignature detection.

name: Dhofar desert (AMADEE-18)
note: Feb 2018 four-week Mars field simulation with crew habitat in the Dhofar desert near Marmul; coordinates approximate.

name: Ramon Crater (AMADEE-20, D-MARS habitat)
note: Erosional makhtesh in the Negev near Mitzpe Ramon; Oct 2021 Mars simulation with 6 analog astronauts; coordinates approximate.

name: Armash (AMADEE-24)
note: March–April 2024 Mars analog mission near Armash village, Ararat province; coordinates approximate.

name: Qaidam Basin – Dalangtan playa
programs: China University of Geosciences Mars analog studies
note: High (~2,700 m), hyperarid salt playas with sulfates, chlorides and yardangs widely cited as China's prime Mars analog; coordinates approximate.

name: Mars Base 1 (C-Space Project), Jinchang Gobi
note: Gobi Desert Mars simulation base ~20 km from Jinchang, Gansu, opened 2019 for training and outreach; coordinates approximate.

source.label: Leonard David – China's Mars Base 1 opens

name: Lonar Crater
note: ~1.8 km impact crater in Deccan flood basalt with an alkaline-saline lake, a rare analog for impacts into basaltic crust as on the Moon and Mars.

name: Tso Kar Valley – HOPE (Ladakh)
programs: ISRO HOPE (Himalayan Outpost for Planetary Exploration)
note: Cold high-altitude (~4,500 m) salt-lake basin with permafrost where ISRO ran its Aug 2025 crewed space analog mission.

source.label: ISRO – Space Analog Mission in Tso Kar Valley

name: Sudbury impact structure
note: ~1.85 Ga, ~130–250 km impact structure with impact melt sheet and Ni-Cu ores; trained Apollo crews in shatter cones and breccias.

name: Mistastin Lake crater
note: ~28 km, ~36 Ma crater in anorthosite, the best terrestrial analog for lunar highland impact melts.

name: Arkaroola (Flinders Ranges)
programs: Mars Society Australia (Arkaroola Mars Robot Challenge)
note: Arid ranges with hydrothermal springs (Paralana), stromatolites and salt lakes proposed for a Mars analog research facility.

name: Pilbara – North Pole Dome (Dresser Formation)
programs: NASA Astrobiology / Mars 2020 science team field training
note: ~3.5 Ga stromatolites and hot-spring deposits, among Earth's oldest life evidence; trains rover teams to recognize biosignatures like those sought in Jezero.

name: Dallol (Danakil Depression)
note: Hyperacid (pH <0), hypersaline, hot hydrothermal salt field below sea level that tests life limits and Martian sulfate/chloride deposition.

name: Death Valley (Badwater / Ubehebe)
note: Hot arid basin with playas, evaporites, alluvial fans and maar craters (Ubehebe) used for Mars rover testing and evaporite studies.

name: Kilauea (Kilauea Iki / Ka'u Desert)
note: Active basaltic shield with fresh flows, fumaroles and lava tubes used for Mars EVA operations (BASALT) and Apollo volcanic training.

name: Teide National Park (Las Cañadas)
programs: ESA ExoMars rover & Raman instrument field tests
note: High-altitude volcanic caldera with basaltic/phonolitic terrains used for ExoMars rover prototype and instrument testing.

name: Aquarius Reef Base (NEEMO)
note: Undersea habitat at ~19 m depth off Key Largo for saturation missions simulating EVA, delayed communications and confined living.

name: HERA (Human Exploration Research Analog), JSC
note: Ground-based isolation habitats at Johnson Space Center for behavioral-health studies of 45-day (HERA) and 378-day (CHAPEA) missions.

name: Erfoud / Sahara (OeWF MARS2013)
note: Feb 2013 OeWF Mars simulation in the northern Sahara near Erfoud with Aouda spacesuit EVAs; coordinates approximate.
